newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: W&H shrs slide after INP bid judged fair.
newsitem.headline: W&H shrs slide after INP bid judged fair.

text.p: Shares in New Zealand publisher Wilson and Horton shed 13 cents to NZ$10.57 on high volume on Friday after the price of Independent Newspapers Plc's takeover offer for the company was declared "fair" by an independent appraiser.

Southpac Corporation Ltd on Thursday said the NZ$10.50 per share offer for Wilson and Horton, made last month by INP through its wholly-owned subsidiary Independent Press Communications, was within Southpac's assessed value range of $10.20 to $11.10 a share.
The slide in the Wilson and Horton share price was a direct result of the Soupthpac report, analysts said.

"There had been speculative buying from investors who were of the opinion that the current bid undervalues Wilson and Horton and that there is a possibility that it will be raised," said Raymond Webb, research analyst at ANZ Securities.
"The likelihood of that is reduced with the recommendation that the offer is fair," he said.

Wilson and Horton shares shot to a high of $10.75 after the takeover offer was announced on September 16, primarily, analysts said, because investors considered the price too low. And despite Southpac's report, analysts believed the offer was still not high enough to induce all Wilson and Horton shareholders to part with their stock.

"Notwithstanding the Southpac conclusion that the offer is fair at $10.50, I think that they (INP) will be very hard pressed to acquire the balance of the company at that level," said John Cairns, head of research at Cavill White Securities.
Analysts said there was still a possibility that the offer price could be raised, but questioned whether INP sought 100 percent control of Wilson and Horton.
"I would think that their primary objective is to get in excess of 50 percent so that they've actually got control of the cash flows," said Cairns.
"But over and above 50 percent, I'm not sure how intent they are. Because if they are intent on doing that, I believe that they would have to offer a higher price."
Wilson and Horton shares would continue to trade at a premium to the offer and had probably bottomed out at around $10.57, analyst said.
By 1.45 p.m. (0145 GMT), Wilson and Horton shares had stabilised at $10.57, down 13 cents on volume of 942,089 shares.
